Send a photo of the broken part, get a quote in 24 hours. We design it, print it and ship it. Nothing is stocked, so every part is made for your model.

### We make and ship it

After you approve, we design, print and ship. Typical lead time is 5 to 10 business days after approval.

## What to expect from us

### Materials we use

- PETG for general parts kept out of heat and direct sun

- ASA for sun and heat

- PA-CF (carbon-fiber nylon) for high loads

- TPU for flexible parts

### What we will not make

- Safety-critical parts such as brakes and steering

- Battery contacts and live electrical parts

- Children's items

- Surfaces that touch food

### Honest lead time

5 to 10 business days after approval, after you approve the quote. Quotes come back within 24 hours on business days. We are not affiliated with any brand, and we do not claim our parts match the original maker's.

## Common questions

### How does PartRevive work?

Send a photo of the broken part, plus the brand and model it came from. We reply with a quote within 24 hours on business days. Once you approve it we design the part, print it, and ship it. Nothing is stocked; every part is made to order.

### How much does a replacement part cost?

Each part page shows a from-price for a typical quote. The final price depends on size, material and quantity, and we confirm it with you before anything is printed.

### How long does it take?

You get a quote within 24 hours on business days. Making and shipping takes 5 to 10 business days after approval.

### Is a 3D-printed part as strong as the original?

It depends on the material and the part. A part in a stronger material such as PA-CF can be stiffer than the original plastic, while a flexible TPU part will not be. We tell you honestly what to expect in the quote, and we do not claim equivalence with the original maker's part.

### What materials do you use?

We print in PETG, ASA, PA-CF (carbon-fibre nylon), TPU. PETG suits general indoor parts, ASA suits sun and heat, PA-CF suits high loads, and TPU suits flexible parts.

### What will you not make?

We do not make safety-critical parts such as brake or steering components, battery contacts or other live electrical parts, children's items, or surfaces that touch food. If you are unsure, ask and we will tell you straight.

# RV window latch replacement, printed in ASA

Short answer: We print replacement RV and camper window latches in ASA, a UV and heat resistant plastic, from your photo or measurements. Send a picture with a coin beside the latch and we quote within 24 hours, from $18 per latch.

From $18

per latch; pairs and multi-packs are quoted lower per unit; final price depends on the shape. Typical quote; final price confirmed before we print.

Lead time: 5 to 10 business days after approval

Quote: within 24 hours on business days

Get a quote

Made to order. You approve the quote before we print anything.

## Fits

- Window latches in the style of Elixir, Hehr and Kinro RV windows (send a photo to confirm the match)
- Many travel trailer, fifth wheel and camper van window latches

Brand names identify fit only. PartRevive is not affiliated with any brand named.

## Why it breaks

RV window latches live in direct sun and heat. Over the years the plastic turns brittle, and a latch that has worked for a decade snaps the day you open the window. Many are sold only as part of a larger window assembly, so a small break can look like a costly repair.

## OEM situation

Typically the original latch is hard to buy on its own and is often sold as part of an assembly. Other printed-latch sellers charge roughly $7 to $24 per latch. We price from $18, and the final figure depends on the shape.

## What we make

We print in ASA because it resists UV and heat far better than ordinary hobby plastics, which matters on a sun-facing window. We match the shape from your photo and, if needed, from the broken pieces. We need a clear photo with a coin or ruler, and the window brand if you know it.

## Specifications

Material | ASA (UV and heat resistant)
Max size | 250 mm
Lead time | 5 to 10 business days after approval
Made | To order from your photo or model number
Price from | $18 (per latch; pairs and multi-packs are quoted lower per unit; final price depends on the shape)

## How to order

- Find the broken latch, or the window it came from, and take it off the window if you can do so safely.
- Send photos on the request page, with a coin or ruler in the shot and the model number if you have it. We reply with a quote within 24 hours on business days.
- Approve the quote and we print the part, usually in 5 to 10 business days after approval, then ship it to you.

Get a quote

## Frequently asked questions

### Will it fit my RV window?

If your latch looks like the Elixir, Hehr or Kinro style, probably. We do not stock parts, so we confirm the match from your photos before quoting and tell you if we are unsure.

### Is a printed part as strong as the original?

We do not claim it matches the original. Printed layers are weakest where they pull apart, so we orient the print so the main load runs along them, and we tell you if a part is a poor candidate. A latch holds a window closed against wind, not a person's weight.

### How do I measure or photograph the part?

Photograph the latch from above and from the side, plus the window frame where it mounts, on a plain background with a coin or ruler beside it. Send the window brand if you know it. If you still have a broken piece, photograph that too.

### Why ASA instead of cheaper plastic?

ASA is made for outdoor sun and heat. Cheaper plastics such as PLA soften in a hot vehicle, so we do not use them for RV parts.

### Can I order a pair or a set for the whole RV?

Yes. Tell us how many windows you have and we quote a lower price per latch for multiples.

# RV cabinet door latch replacement

Short answer: We print replacement RV cabinet door latches in ASA, including shapes that are discontinued, from your photo or part number. Send a picture with a coin for scale and we quote within 24 hours, from $22.

From $22

per latch; multi-packs quoted lower per unit. Typical quote; final price confirmed before we print.

Lead time: 5 to 10 business days after approval

Quote: within 24 hours on business days

Get a quote

Made to order. You approve the quote before we print anything.

## Fits

- Cabinet latches in the style of the Newmar 020658A (send a photo to confirm)
- Many motorhome and travel trailer overhead and galley cabinet latches

Brand names identify fit only. PartRevive is not affiliated with any brand named.

## Why it breaks

Cabinet latches flex every time the door opens, and years of heat cycles in a parked RV make the plastic brittle. When one cracks, the door swings open on the road. Some makers have discontinued the shape, so a direct replacement may not exist.

## OEM situation

The Newmar 020658A latch is discontinued. A printed version of it sells for about $24 elsewhere. We price from $22 for a typical simple latch, and the final figure depends on the shape.

## What we make

We print in ASA, which holds up to the heat inside a closed RV in summer. We copy the profile from your photo, your broken latch or its mounting holes. We need a clear photo with a coin or ruler, the RV make and year if you know them, and any number stamped on the part.

## Specifications

Material | ASA (UV and heat resistant)
Max size | 250 mm
Lead time | 5 to 10 business days after approval
Made | To order from your photo or model number
Price from | $22 (per latch; multi-packs quoted lower per unit)

## How to order

- Take the broken latch off the cabinet, or photograph it in place if the door is still on.
- Send photos on the request page, with a coin or ruler in the shot and the model number if you have it. We reply with a quote within 24 hours on business days.
- Approve the quote and we print the part, usually in 5 to 10 business days after approval, then ship it to you.

Get a quote

## Frequently asked questions

### My latch is discontinued. Can you still make it?

Usually, yes, if we can see the shape and the mounting points. Send photos of both sides and we tell you in the quote if anything looks unmakeable.

### Is a printed part as strong as the original?

We do not claim it matches the original. Printed layers are weakest where they pull apart, so we orient the print so the main load runs along them, and we tell you if a part is a poor candidate.

### How do I measure or photograph the part?

Photograph the front, back and edge of the latch, and the cutout it sits in, on a plain background with a coin or ruler beside it. Send the RV make and year if you know them, and any number stamped on the part. If you still have a broken piece, photograph that too.

### Will it keep a cabinet door shut while driving?

We cannot promise it performs like the original. A latch holds a door only as well as its design and the cabinet allow, so a spare latch is a sensible order for heavy cabinets.

### Do you make metal strikers and screws?

No. We make the plastic latch parts only.

# Whirlpool fridge door bin replacement (also fits KitchenAid styles)

Short answer: We print replacement Whirlpool and KitchenAid style refrigerator door bins and bin holders to order, matched to your model number and photos. Send them and we quote within 24 hours, from $65.

From $65

per bin or holder; price depends on size. Typical quote; final price confirmed before we print.

Lead time: 5 to 10 business days after approval

Quote: within 24 hours on business days

Get a quote

Made to order. You approve the quote before we print anything.

## Fits

- Whirlpool refrigerator door bins and holders (confirm by model number)
- KitchenAid refrigerator door bins and holders (confirm by model number)

Brand names identify fit only. PartRevive is not affiliated with any brand named.

## Why it breaks

Fridge door bins carry heavy jars and bottles, and cold plastic gets brittle. The holder tabs, the small parts that hook the bin to the door, are what usually break first, and often the whole shelf cracks along a corner.

## OEM situation

Originals are often sold as a bin-plus-holder set and can cost around $200. We price made-to-order bins from $65.

## What we make

We print in PETG, which stays tough at fridge temperatures. We rebuild the broken bin or holder to your measurements. We do not make food-contact claims, so we suggest the bin for jars, bottles and packaged food rather than loose items. We need your model number, found on a sticker inside the fridge, and photos with a ruler.

## Specifications

Material | PETG
Max size | 250 mm
Lead time | 5 to 10 business days after approval
Made | To order from your photo or model number
Price from | $65 (per bin or holder; price depends on size)

## How to order

- Find the model number on the sticker inside the fridge, usually on the upper wall or a side wall.
- Send photos on the request page, with a coin or ruler in the shot and the model number if you have it. We reply with a quote within 24 hours on business days.
- Approve the quote and we print the part, usually in 5 to 10 business days after approval, then ship it to you.

Get a quote

## Frequently asked questions

### Where is my fridge model number?

Usually on a sticker inside the fresh-food compartment, on a side wall or near the top. Photograph it and send it with the broken part.

### Is a printed part as strong as the original?

We do not claim it matches the original. Printed layers are weakest where they pull apart, so we orient the print so the main load runs along them, and we tell you if a part is a poor candidate. Door bins carry jars and bottles, so tell us what you plan to store and we tell you whether the bin is a poor candidate for that load.

### How do I measure or photograph the part?

Photograph the bin from above and from the side, and the door where it mounts, on a plain background with a coin or ruler beside it. Also send the fridge model number from the sticker inside the fresh-food compartment. If you still have a broken piece, photograph that too.

### Is the bin food safe?

We make no food-contact claims. Use it for sealed or packaged items and do not put loose food directly against it.

### Can you make just the small holder?

Yes. If only the holder is broken we quote just that, which costs less than a whole bin.

# Samsung fridge door bin replacement

Short answer: We print replacement Samsung style refrigerator door bins to order, matched to your model number and photos. Send them and we quote within 24 hours, from $55.

From $55

per bin; price depends on size. Typical quote; final price confirmed before we print.

Lead time: 5 to 10 business days after approval

Quote: within 24 hours on business days

Get a quote

Made to order. You approve the quote before we print anything.

## Fits

- Samsung refrigerator door bins (confirm by model number)

Brand names identify fit only. PartRevive is not affiliated with any brand named.

## Why it breaks

A door bin that holds a gallon of milk takes a lot of weight at its corners and lower edge. Cold, aging plastic cracks there, and the bin drops or sags. Replacing the whole door is not an option, so the bin is the part people hunt for.

## OEM situation

Original Samsung bins typically cost $115 to $140 and are often out of stock. We price from $55 for a typical bin, and the final figure depends on size.

## What we make

We print in PETG, which stays tough in the cold. We rebuild the bin to your photos and measurements. We do not make food-contact claims, so use it for jars, bottles and packaged items. We need the model number from the sticker inside the fridge and photos with a ruler.

## Specifications

Material | PETG
Max size | 250 mm
Lead time | 5 to 10 business days after approval
Made | To order from your photo or model number
Price from | $55 (per bin; price depends on size)

## How to order

- Find the model number sticker inside the fridge, then photograph the broken bin and the door it mounts to.
- Send photos on the request page, with a coin or ruler in the shot and the model number if you have it. We reply with a quote within 24 hours on business days.
- Approve the quote and we print the part, usually in 5 to 10 business days after approval, then ship it to you.

Get a quote

## Frequently asked questions

### Where is my Samsung model number?

Look on a sticker inside the fridge compartment, on a side wall or near the top. Send a photo of it with the damaged bin.

### Is a printed part as strong as the original?

We do not claim it matches the original. Printed layers are weakest where they pull apart, so we orient the print so the main load runs along them, and we tell you if a part is a poor candidate. We reinforce load-bearing corners where the original design allows.

### How do I measure or photograph the part?

Photograph the bin from the front, the side and the underside, and the clips or rails that hold it, on a plain background with a coin or ruler beside it. Also send the fridge model number from the sticker inside the fridge compartment. If you still have a broken piece, photograph that too.

### Is the bin food safe?

We make no food-contact claims. Keep loose food off it and use it for packaged goods and bottles.

### Will the bin look the same as the original?

Printed does not mean identical. It is made to fit the same space, the surface shows fine print lines, and the color is the nearest we can offer, not an exact match.

# DeWalt TSTAK latch replacement, printed pair

Short answer: We print replacement latch clips that fit DeWalt TSTAK toolboxes in PETG, or in carbon-fiber nylon (PA-CF) for harder use. Send a photo of the broken latch and we quote within 24 hours, from $12 for a pair.

From $12

per pair in PETG; PA-CF is quoted higher; larger sets quoted lower per clip. Typical quote; final price confirmed before we print.

Lead time: 5 to 10 business days after approval

Quote: within 24 hours on business days

Get a quote

Made to order. You approve the quote before we print anything.

## Fits

- DeWalt TSTAK stackable toolbox latches and clips (send a photo to confirm your box)

Brand names identify fit only. PartRevive is not affiliated with any brand named.

## Why it breaks

TSTAK latches get snapped when boxes are stacked and lifted by the handle, or when a lid is slammed in the cold. The latch is a small part on a large, otherwise sound box, so people end up with a good box that will not close.

## OEM situation

An original latch is about $22 on eBay. A printed 2-pack sells for $9.95 elsewhere. We price from $12 a pair and quote based on the version of the latch.

## What we make

We print PETG for everyday toolboxes and PA-CF, carbon-fiber filled nylon, when the box takes hard use. Printing the latch with layers running along the load path helps reduce the chance of it snapping the same way again, though we cannot guarantee how long it lasts. We need a photo of the broken latch beside a coin and one of the matching spot on the box.

## Specifications

Material | PETG standard, PA-CF on request
Max size | 250 mm
Lead time | 5 to 10 business days after approval
Made | To order from your photo or model number
Price from | $12 (per pair in PETG; PA-CF is quoted higher; larger sets quoted lower per clip)

## How to order

- Photograph the broken latch, or the empty latch position on the box, with a coin in the shot.
- Send photos on the request page, with a coin or ruler in the shot and the model number if you have it. We reply with a quote within 24 hours on business days.
- Approve the quote and we print the part, usually in 5 to 10 business days after approval, then ship it to you.

Get a quote

## Frequently asked questions

### Will it fit my TSTAK box?

If your box looks like a DeWalt TSTAK, we match it from photos. Tell us which box size you have and we confirm the fit before printing.

### Is a printed part as strong as the original?

We do not claim it matches the original. Printed layers are weakest where they pull apart, so we orient the print so the main load runs along them, and we tell you if a part is a poor candidate. If the latch has snapped repeatedly, ask for PA-CF, which is stiffer and tougher.

### How do I measure or photograph the part?

Photograph the latch from the front, the side and the underside, plus the post it clips onto, on a plain background with a coin or ruler beside it. Send the box model if you know it. If you still have a broken piece, photograph that too.

### Is PETG strong enough for a loaded toolbox?

For ordinary use, usually. For heavy tools or a box that gets dropped, choose PA-CF and let us know the loaded weight.

### Can I order a set for several boxes?

Yes. Give us the number of latches you need and we quote a lower price per clip.

# Milwaukee Packout drawer latch replacement

Short answer: We print replacement drawer latches that fit Milwaukee Packout organizers in PETG, or PA-CF for harder use. Send a photo of the broken latch and we quote within 24 hours, from $14.

From $14

per latch in PETG; PA-CF is quoted higher; multiples quoted lower per unit. Typical quote; final price confirmed before we print.

Lead time: 5 to 10 business days after approval

Quote: within 24 hours on business days

Get a quote

Made to order. You approve the quote before we print anything.

## Fits

- Milwaukee Packout drawer organizer latches (send a photo to confirm your model)

Brand names identify fit only. PartRevive is not affiliated with any brand named.

## Why it breaks

Packout drawers get slammed, dropped and used in cold trucks, and the small latch is the weak point. When it cracks, the drawer slides open in transit while the rest of the organizer is fine.

## OEM situation

A non-printed aftermarket latch is listed at $8.99. We do not try to beat that for a simple generic latch. We are for cases where the stock part does not fit or is out of stock.

## What we make

## OEM situation

## What we make

This is the main service. You photograph the part, we reply within 24 hours with a yes, a no, or a question. ## Why it breaks

The rubber pull latch tears, or its pin hole stretches until it slips off, after years of sun and use. The cooler is fine but will not stay shut.

## OEM situation

An official 2-pack is about $17 at one retailer, while one reseller lists a 2-pack at $61.39. Latches are sold in sets, and the larger Tundra 85, 120 and 155 coolers use three. We print a single latch or a full set and price from $14.

## What we make

We print in TPU, a flexible plastic that stretches and springs back, so the latch can still pull over the lid lug. The pin hole size matters most, so we need a photo of the old latch beside a coin and one of the lug it hooks onto. We do not claim bear-resistance or any special rating.

We do not claim it matches the original. TPU is flexible, so it bends rather than snaps, but it can stretch or wear over time. We tell you if your latch looks like a poor candidate.

### Will it hold up in the sun?

We do not give TPU a UV rating, and sun slowly wears any flexible plastic. If the cooler lives in strong sun, tell us when you order.

### Is it safe for food?

The latch sits on the outside of the cooler and does not touch food. We make no food-contact safety claim, so we do not recommend it for any part that touches food or drink.

## Why it breaks

The small latch tab or spring arm on the detergent door snaps, so the door will not stay shut or will not pop open at the right moment in the cycle. The part lives in hot water and detergent and flexes every wash. A tiny broken tab then makes the whole dispenser look useless.

## OEM situation

Individual repair parts are often discontinued, so the usual replacement is the full dispenser assembly. Whirlpool part WPW10224428 is listed at about $58.95 to $60.52, and a KitchenAid assembly, WPW10224430, at about $138.28. A latch-only part, WP99001291, exists for some models. Other owners have reprinted their own latches rather than buy a whole door.

## What we make

We print the latch in PETG, sized to your dispenser from your photos, typically around 35 x 15 x 10 mm. It touches detergent and hot water but not food. We do not claim dishwasher-safe certification or OEM equivalence, and spring-action fit varies by model, so we confirm it with you before printing. We need photos of the broken latch and the dispenser, with a coin or ruler in the shot, plus the model number.

## Frequently asked questions

### Will it fit my dishwasher?

### Is a printed latch as strong as the original?

We do not claim it matches the original. PETG is tough and slightly flexible, which suits a spring arm, but it can still fatigue after many cycles. We orient the print so the flex runs along the layers and tell you if a part is a poor candidate.

### Can it handle hot water and detergent?

We cannot promise how it ages in repeated hot cycles. It touches detergent and hot water but not food. We do not claim dishwasher-safe certification, and a latch near a heating element is a poor fit for PETG.

### How do I photograph or measure the latch?

Photograph the latch and the door from the front, the side and the inside on a plain background with a coin or ruler beside them. Also send the model number, usually on a sticker on the door edge or the tub frame. Keep any broken pieces and photograph them too.

### Is it cheaper than a new dispenser?

Often, if only the latch is broken and a latch-only part is not available for your model. Full dispenser assemblies are listed at about $58.95 and up, and our latch starts from $24. The quote depends on your model.

Brand names identify fit only. PartRevive is not affiliated with any brand named.

## Why it breaks

The latch hook or its pin cracks, or the small spring tab snaps, after years of opening and closing under load. The case itself is usually fine, but one dead latch means it no longer closes tight.

## OEM situation

Single latches are typically not sold separately. Genuine latches usually come as a handle-and-latch set from resellers such as ColorCase. We print one latch and price from $16.

## What we make

We print in PA-CF, carbon-fiber filled nylon, because a latch hook takes repeated load and PA-CF is stiff and tough. We orient the print so the main load runs along the layers. ### Is a printed latch as strong as the original?

We do not claim it matches the original. PA-CF is stiff and tough. Printed layers are weakest where they pull apart, so we orient the print so the main load runs along them. We tell you if your latch is a poor candidate.

### Will the case still be waterproof?

We make no waterproof or ingress-rating claim. A case seal depends on the latch holding the lid firmly, so a good-fitting latch helps, but we cannot promise any seal level.

### Can it live outdoors in the sun?

We do not give a UV rating for PA-CF. If the case sits in strong sun all day, tell us and we will discuss options, such as ASA.

- Matched to a splined shaft or a 1/2 in shaft, from your measurements

Brand names identify fit only. PartRevive is not affiliated with any brand named.

## Why it breaks

Plastic crank knobs strip where they grip the shaft, so the handle spins without opening the vent. The knobs sit in the sun for years and turn brittle. The fit depends on the exact spline or shaft size, which varies between makers.

## OEM situation

A Ventline operator with crank, BVD0462-00, was listed at $23.14 and out of stock. Spline patterns differ between makers, so a generic knob may not fit. We price from $16.

## What we make

## Frequently asked questions

### Will it fit my vent?

### Is a printed knob as strong as the original?

We do not claim it matches the original. Printed layers are weakest where they pull apart, so we orient the print so the main load runs along them. We tell you if a part is a poor candidate.

### How do I measure the shaft?

### My shaft is splined. Does that matter?

Yes. Spline patterns differ between makers. A clear straight-on photo of the shaft end is the most useful thing you can send.

Yes. Tell us how many vents you have and we quote a lower price per knob.

- Bucket-seat console versions; we confirm from your photo whether the latch or the lid is the broken part

Brand names identify fit only. PartRevive is not affiliated with any brand named.

## Why it breaks

The console latch breaks and the lid will not stay shut, so it flaps open over bumps and corners. It is a small part, but the console is used every drive. People often cannot tell whether the latch or the lid itself has failed.

## OEM situation

A cheap fix exists: one retailer lists an aftermarket 2-pack of latches (GM 20864151/53/54) for $8.99, and a single latch for $25.95. If the cheap latch fits your truck, buy it. A made-to-fit printed part makes sense when your year or color does not match, the part is discontinued, or the latch keeps breaking and you want a different material.

## What we make

We print PETG, which holds up in a warm cabin where PLA softens, and we can use ASA if the vehicle sits in strong sun. We do not use PLA for car interiors. We need a photo of the old latch or the empty position, with a coin or ruler in the shot, and your year and model. Interior trim only; we do not make airbag, seatbelt, brake, steering, lighting or fuel parts.

### Is a printed latch as strong as the original?

We do not claim it matches the original. Printed layers are weakest where they pull apart, so we orient the print so the main load runs along them. We tell you if the part is a poor candidate.

### Will it handle heat in a parked truck?

PLA softens in a hot car, so we do not use it. We print PETG for cabins and can use ASA if the vehicle sits in strong sun.

# Can this broken plastic part be 3D printed? A buyer's checklist

By PartRevive · 2026-10-21

Short answer: Most broken plastic parts under 250 mm can be 3D printed if they are not food-contact, not safety-critical and not exposed to high heat. If the part sits in the sun or heat we use ASA, and for high load we use carbon-fiber nylon (PA-CF).

## The short answer

Many broken plastic parts can be 3D printed, but not all. A part is a good candidate when it is small enough, made of plastic, and not asked to do a job where failure hurts someone. This page is the checklist we use before we quote.

## Check 1: is it small enough?

Our printers handle parts up to 250 mm in any direction. That covers knobs, clips, latches, hinges, brackets, bins and trim pieces. A large panel or a full shelf is outside that limit, though sometimes it can be made in sections. Measure the longest side with a ruler and tell us.

## Check 2: is it plastic?

We print plastic only. A metal part that has a plastic cap or sleeve is fine, because the cap can be printed. Metal gears, springs and screws we do not make. If the original part mixes materials, tell us which piece is broken.

## Check 3: how hot does it get?

Heat is the most common reason a printed part fails. Ordinary hobby plastics such as PLA soften in a hot car. We do not use PLA. For parts in the sun, a vehicle or near warm machinery, we print in ASA, which resists UV and heat. If the part touches high heat, such as an oven, a heater or an engine bay, it is not a good candidate, and we say so.

## Check 4: what is it carrying?

Strength depends on the load, and on how the part is printed. Printed layers are weakest where they pull apart, so we orient the print so the main load runs along them. We have four materials to match the job.

Material | Best for | Notes

PETG | General use, cold, fridge and toolbox parts | Tough; for hot places we use ASA

ASA | Sun, heat, car and RV parts | Our choice for outdoor and vehicle use

PA-CF (carbon-fiber nylon) | High load, repeated stress | Stiff and strong; costs more

TPU | Flexible parts: seals, feet, bumpers | Soft and bendy

## Check 5: could failure hurt someone?

This is a firm line. We do not print safety-critical parts: brakes, battery contacts, seat belt parts, child items, or anything where a break could injure. We also do not touch electrical parts. We can print the plastic knob or trigger on an appliance, but not a switch or wiring. If you are not sure, ask and we will answer honestly.

## Check 6: will it touch food or drink?

We make no food-contact claims. A part that sits where food or drink touches it directly, like a cup or a scoop, is not something we print. Parts such as a fridge door bin that hold packaged items are different, but we still make no certification claims.

## What a good candidate looks like

- A knob, latch, clip or bin under 250 mm.

- Not near high heat, or in ASA if it is warm.

- Discontinued or sold only as an expensive assembly.

- Photographed clearly with a coin or ruler beside it.

## Examples we make

See our pages for an RV window latch, a DeWalt TSTAK latch, a Whirlpool or KitchenAid fridge door bin, and a dryer knob. If your part is not on the list, use the custom part from a photo service.

## What it costs and how long it takes

Custom parts start from $35, including design time for simple parts. Complex shapes are quoted individually. After you approve the quote, printing and shipping usually take 5 to 10 business days. We quote within 24 hours on business days.

## When we say no

We would rather decline than quote a part that will not work. Common reasons we say no: the part is safety-critical, the part must meet a food-contact standard, the part faces an oven or engine bay, the part is bigger than 250 mm, or the original is a metal part we cannot copy in plastic. When we say no, we explain why in a sentence or two, so you can look for another route.

## What happens if the part is borderline

Sometimes a part is possible but risky, for example a clip near a warm motor. In that case we tell you the risk, suggest ASA or PA-CF, and let you decide. You are never charged until you approve a quote. A small test print of the critical area is sometimes the cheapest way to check the fit before the whole part is made.

## Why photos beat descriptions

A description such as a small white clip with two holes fits a hundred different parts. A photo with a coin beside it fits one. That is why every quote starts with a photo, and why our guide on photographing a broken part is worth a minute of your time.

## Next step

Send a photo through the request page. If we think the part is a poor fit, we say so.

## Need a replacement made?

Send a photo and the model number and we will quote within 24 hours on business days.

Request a quote

## Frequently asked questions

### What is the biggest part you can print?

Up to 250 mm. Larger parts may be possible in sections, which we quote individually.

### Can you print a part that gets hot?

In ASA, for moderate heat such as sun or a car interior. We do not print parts for ovens, heaters or engine bays.

### Do you print food-contact parts?

No. We make no food-contact claims.

### Do you print brakes or safety parts?

No. We do not print safety-critical parts or touch electrical parts.

### What does a custom part cost?

From $35, including design time for simple parts. Complex shapes are quoted individually.

## Related parts

-

From $35

# Broken center console latch: your options and what they cost

By PartRevive · 2026-10-21

Short answer: A center console latch usually breaks because its small plastic hook is thin, loaded every time the lid closes, and baked by cabin heat. You can buy an aftermarket latch, ask a dealer, or have a made-to-fit latch printed in PETG or ASA, which we quote within 24 hours on business days.

## The short answer

When a console lid will not stay shut, the part that failed is almost always the latch itself: a small plastic hook with a couple of retention tabs. The lid, the hinge and the console body are usually fine. That is good news, because the latch is a small, cheap part when you can find it on its own.

The trouble is finding it. This guide covers why the hook breaks, what the three common routes cost, and when a printed latch is worth ordering.

## Why the little hook breaks

A console latch does a hard job in a small package. The hook catches a striker every time you close the lid, and the lid is often leaned on, used as an armrest or pushed shut with a full hand.

- Thin geometry. The hook and its tabs are small, so a little bending load concentrates at the root.

- Repeated cycles. Hundreds of closings flex the same spot until it cracks.

- Heat. A parked car cabin in summer gets very hot, and plastic that is stiff in spring can soften and creep by August.

- Age. Old plastic loses toughness, so the tab that survived ten years snaps on the eleventh.

## Why PLA fails in a hot cabin

PLA is the easiest plastic to print, which is why many free latch designs use it. It also softens at low temperatures compared with other print plastics, and a closed vehicle in the sun can pass that point. We make vehicle parts in PETG or ASA, never PLA.

### PETG or ASA?

PETG is tough, slightly flexible and a sound choice for a console latch in most climates. ASA is made for sun and heat, so we suggest it for a vehicle that lives in a hot place or parks outdoors all day.

## Three ways to fix it

Here is how the routes compare, using the prices we could confirm.

Option | Typical price | Fit | Material | Lead time

Dealer part | Varies by dealer | Matches the original | Original | Varies

Aftermarket latch | $8.99 for a 2-pack of GM-style latches, or $25.95 for a single, on Walmart | Good if the number and year match | Molded plastic | Varies

Made-to-fit printed latch | From $18 for the Tacoma, from $19 for the Silverado and Sierra | Matched to your photo | PETG, or ASA for hot cabins | 5 to 10 business days after approval

If a $8.99 2-pack fits your truck, that is hard to beat on price, and we would buy it. A printed latch makes sense when the aftermarket part does not fit your year, is out of stock, or has already broken the same way.

## Toyota Tacoma consoles

Molded Tacoma latches are sold by Extreme Terrain in beige for 2009 to 2012 and in gray for 2005 to 2012, and a Home Depot listing covers the 2005 to 2012 gray latch. Original part numbers vary by year, so check your year and color before you order. We list a Tacoma console latch made from your photo.

## Silverado, Sierra and related trucks

The 2007 to 2013 GM trucks and SUVs with the bucket-seat console share a latch that the Walmart 2-pack lists as GM 20864151, 20864153 and 20864154. Photograph both the latch and the lid so we can tell whether the latch or the lid catch is the part that failed. Our Silverado and Sierra console latch page has the details.

## How to tell what has broken

- Open the lid and look at the latch body for a missing hook or snapped tabs.

- Check the striker on the console base; if it is bent or loose, a new latch alone will not hold.

- Press the release button and see whether the latch still moves under its spring.

- Look for cracks in the plastic around the latch pocket.

## What to photograph

Send a close photo of the broken latch from the front and back, with a coin or ruler beside it. Add a photo of the latch pocket in the lid, the striker on the console, and your vehicle year and trim. Use the request page to send them. If you have a related trim part, such as a cracked sun visor clip, include it in the same request and we can quote both together.

## What we do not promise

A printed latch is not an original part, and we are not affiliated with any vehicle maker. We do not claim it is equal to the factory part. A console latch is a convenience item, not a safety part, and we will not quote parts for brakes, airbags or other safety systems. Quotes arrive within 24 hours on business days, and parts ship 5 to 10 business days after approval.

## Need a replacement made?

Send a photo and the model number and we will quote within 24 hours on business days.

Request a quote

## Frequently asked questions

### Why does my console latch keep breaking?

The hook is small, flexes every time the lid closes, and the plastic ages and softens in a hot cabin. Heat, age and repeated closing all wear the hook, so the material and the thickness of the hook matter.

### Can I buy just the latch from a dealer?

Not always. Availability varies by dealer, so ask for the part number for your year first.

### Why not print it in PLA?

PLA can soften in a hot cabin. We use PETG or ASA instead.

### Is a printed latch cheaper than an aftermarket 2-pack?

No. A 2-pack was listed at $8.99 on Walmart. Our printed latches start from $18, and they suit cases where the stock part does not fit.

### Which years do you cover?

We work from your photo and year. Typical fits are Tacoma 2005 to 2012 and GM trucks 2007 to 2013, but send a photo if yours is different.

# Fixing a broken cooler latch or hinge: Yeti, RTIC, Igloo, Coleman

By PartRevive · 2026-10-21

Short answer: A cooler latch or hinge usually fails at the pin hole, where a rubber latch stretches or a plastic hinge splits. Stock sets cost about $10 to $17 when they fit, and a printed TPU latch or PETG hinge makes sense when you only need one piece or the set does not match.

## The short answer

Coolers outlive their small parts. The body keeps working for a decade, while a rubber pull latch tears or a plastic hinge cracks at the pin. Before you buy a whole new cooler, check whether the part is sold as a set you can afford, and whether a printed one-off would be a better fit.

## Pull latches: Yeti and RTIC style

The rubber pull latch on a hard cooler wears out in two ways. The rubber tears, or the hole that sits over the pin stretches until the latch slips off. Both come from years of sun and daily pulling.

Official latch sets are sold in packs. A Yeti Tundra 2-pack was listed at about $17 at Farm and Fleet, while one reseller listed the same 2-pack at $61.39, so shop around. Larger Tundra sizes such as the 85, 120 and 155 use three latches, so a 2-pack may leave you one short.

### When a printed TPU latch makes sense

TPU is a flexible plastic, so it bends instead of snapping. We suggest it when you need a single latch rather than a pack, when one has stretched at the pin hole, or when a set is out of stock. Other small shops print latches for popular coolers too, so a printed latch is not a new idea; our advantage is matching your cooler from a photo and your measurements. We do not claim it equals the original, and we do not make any claim about resistance to animals or rough handling.

## Lid hinges: Igloo and Coleman style

Plastic hinges on Igloo and Coleman coolers typically crack or split at the pin. Igloo hinges are reported to split from stress after a few years. The good news is that stock sets are cheap:

- Igloo Universal Hinge Set: about $10 to $12 per pair at Sportsman's Warehouse.

- Coleman hinge set of four: about $10.43 at Walmart.

- Hinge for a 150 to 165 quart Igloo: $35.99 from one seller.

If a universal set bolts on and the lid sits right, buy it. A printed PETG hinge is worth asking about when the universal hinge does not line up with your screw holes, when you have an older model, or when a large cooler needs a bigger hinge. We focus on exact-fit matching from your photo.

## Pelican-style case latches

Hard cases use a hook, pin and spring tab that can crack. Single latches are typically not sold on their own. ColorCase sells genuine handle-and-latch sets for the 1510. For a printed latch we use PA-CF, a stiff carbon-fiber nylon. We make no claim about sealing or water protection; how a case seals depends on how firmly the latch holds the lid, and we do not promise an IP rating.

## OEM, aftermarket and printed compared

Option | Typical price | Fit | Material | Lead time

Yeti latch 2-pack | About $17, one reseller $61.39 | Matches the original | Rubber | Varies

Igloo or Coleman hinge set | About $10 to $12 per pair | Good if the universal set fits | Plastic | Varies

Printed latch (TPU) | From $14 | Matched to your photo | TPU | 5 to 10 business days after approval

Printed hinge (PETG) | From $14 | Matched to your photo | PETG | 5 to 10 business days after approval

Printed case latch (PA-CF) | From $16 | Matched to your photo | PA-CF | 5 to 10 business days after approval

## What to measure

- Pin diameter. Measure the post or pin the latch hooks over, in millimeters. Pin-hole size is the critical number for a flexible latch.

- Screw spacing. Measure center to center between the two screw holes on a hinge or latch plate.

- Hinge width and thickness. Note the overall length and how thick the hinge is where it meets the pin.

- Number of latches. Count how many your cooler or case has, so we can quote a full set if you want one.

If you cannot measure, a photo with a coin or ruler beside the part is enough for a first quote.

## What to photograph

Take the broken part on a plain surface, then the spot on the cooler where it mounts. Include the pin or the hinge pocket from the side and from above. Add any model name on the cooler if you can read it. Send everything on the request page.

## Our related part pages

See the cooler lid latch page for pull latches, the cooler lid hinge page for Igloo, Coleman and Rubbermaid style hinges, and the hard case latch page for Pelican-style cases.

## What we do not promise

A printed part is not an original, and we are not affiliated with Yeti, RTIC, Igloo, Coleman or Pelican. We do not claim equal strength, any sealing performance or any food-related approval. If a part is a poor candidate for printing, we say so rather than quote it. Quotes arrive within 24 hours on business days, and parts ship 5 to 10 business days after approval.

## Need a replacement made?

Send a photo and the model number and we will quote within 24 hours on business days.

Request a quote

## Frequently asked questions

### How much is an official Yeti latch set?

A Tundra 2-pack was listed at about $17 at Farm and Fleet, and one reseller listed it at $61.39. Larger Tundra sizes use three latches.

### Why does a cooler hinge split?

Plastic hinges typically crack at the pin after years of stress and sun. A reviewer reports Igloo hinges splitting after a few years.

### When is a printed latch better than a stock set?

When you need only one latch, the set is out of stock, or the stretched pin hole means the new part must be matched to your cooler.

### What should I measure?

The pin diameter and the center-to-center screw spacing. A photo with a coin or ruler works if you cannot measure.

### Do you make Pelican-style case latches?

Yes, in PA-CF from a photo. We do not make claims about sealing or water protection.

## Related parts

-

# Why a DeWalt TSTAK latch keeps breaking, and what to do

By PartRevive · 2026-10-21

Short answer: A DeWalt TSTAK latch usually breaks from side loads, cold plastic and lifting a stack by the handle. A replacement printed with layers aligned to the load, in PETG or carbon-fiber nylon (PA-CF), can reduce the chance of repeat breaks, though we cannot guarantee lifespan. We quote a PETG pair from $12 (PA-CF quoted higher) within 24 hours.

## The short answer

If a TSTAK latch keeps snapping, the plastic is probably not at fault alone. It is the load direction, the cold, or the way boxes are stacked and carried. A stronger material helps, and so does printing the latch with its layers lined up to the load.

## What breaks a TSTAK latch

### Side loads

The latch is designed to pull a lid down, not to take a sideways knock. A box dropped on its corner or a lid slammed shut puts a bending load on the hook, and plastic hooks snap at the root.

### Cold

Plastics get more brittle as the temperature drops. A truck bed or garage in winter turns a latch that survived all summer into one that snaps with one knock.

### Stacking and carrying

When boxes are stacked and lifted by one handle, the latches between them carry the weight of every box below. A latch built to hold a lid then holds a stack.

### Layer lines in printed parts

If you have a printed latch that broke, look at the break. A flat, straight break along a layer line means the part was printed with layers across the load. This usually points to the print orientation rather than the material. We orient latches so the layers run with the main load.

## Original, aftermarket or printed

Option | Typical price | Availability | Fit risk

Original latch | About $22 on eBay | Usually available, but check the version | Low

Printed 2-pack from other sellers | As low as $9.95 | Usually available | Medium; material and print orientation vary

Printed here in PETG or PA-CF | From $12 per pair in PETG; PA-CF quoted higher | Made to order, 5 to 10 business days after approval | Low to medium; matched from your photo

The cheapest option is not always wrong. If a stock latch fits and your box rarely sees hard use, buy it. Our printed pair makes sense if the latches keep breaking or you want PA-CF.

## PETG or PA-CF?

PETG is a tough everyday plastic and suits a toolbox that lives in a garage or van. PA-CF is nylon with carbon fiber, stiffer and more resistant to repeated stress, and a better choice for a box that is dropped, stacked high or used on a job site. Ask for it in your request. PA-CF costs more than PETG, and we say so in the quote.

## A quick way to judge a broken latch

Pick up the broken pieces and look at the fracture. A clean break at the base of the hook usually means a sideways knock or cold plastic. A break across the middle of the arm, after the latch had bent for a while, points to a latch that is too thin or too soft for the load. Both tell us where to add material in the new one, so send a photo of the fracture along with the latch.

### When to replace the whole lid or box

If the box body has cracks around the latch post, a new latch will not last, because the post is what holds it. We cannot repair the box itself, and we tell you when a new latch is not the answer. Often, though, the box is sound and only the small part has failed, which is why people keep a spare pair in the box.

### Ordering several

If you have more than one box, the latches are all the same age and have seen the same use. Ordering a set at once lowers the price per clip and saves a second round of shipping. Tell us how many boxes you have when you send your request.

## How to stop the next break

- Lift stacked boxes by their own handles when you can, not by the top handle alone.

- Latch the lid with a gentle push, not a slam.

- Do not stack beyond the rated height.

- Keep a spare latch pair in the toolbox itself.

## What we need to make a latch

Photograph the broken latch, or the empty latch position, with a coin beside it. Add a view of the post it clips onto. Send them through the request page. For details on pricing, see the TSTAK latch page. If you also have a Milwaukee box, the Packout drawer latch page covers that one.

## What we do not promise

We do not claim a printed latch is equal to the original, and we are not affiliated with DeWalt. Printed layers are weakest where they pull apart, so we orient the print so the main load runs along them. If a latch is a poor candidate for printing, we say so rather than quote it.

## Need a replacement made?

Send a photo and the model number and we will quote within 24 hours on business days.

Request a quote

## Frequently asked questions

### Why does my TSTAK latch keep snapping?

Usually side loads, cold plastic, and carrying a stack by one handle. A latch printed with layers aligned to the load and made in PA-CF may last longer.

### Is a printed latch cheaper than the original?

An original is about $22 on eBay and we quote a printed pair from $12. Other sellers list printed 2-packs as low as $9.95.

### Should I choose PETG or PA-CF?

PETG for ordinary use, PA-CF for boxes that are dropped, stacked high or used on job sites.

### What photo do you need?

The broken latch and the latch position on the box, with a coin or ruler in the picture.

## Related parts

# Cracked fridge door bin: your options and what each costs

By PartRevive · 2026-10-21

Short answer: A broken fridge door bin can be replaced with an original part, a used part, or a part printed to order. Originals are the surest fit but often cost $115 to $200 or more and are sometimes out of stock, while a printed bin typically costs less and is made to your model.

## The short answer

You have three realistic options for a cracked refrigerator door bin: buy the original part, buy a used one, or have one printed to order. There is no single best choice. It depends on how much the original costs for your model, whether it is in stock, and how much fit risk you can accept.

## Why door bins break

A door bin carries jars, bottles and a gallon of milk on a thin plastic shelf, and cold makes plastic more brittle. Cracks start at the corners, along the lower edge and at the small holder tabs that hook the bin to the door. Once a tab breaks, the bin sags or falls out.

The fridge itself is rarely the problem. The compressor, cooling and shelves may all be fine, so a single plastic part decides whether you keep the appliance or replace it.

## Option 1: the original part

An original bin is the safest bet for fit, because it is the part the fridge was designed for. The trouble is price and supply. A Whirlpool bin plus holder can cost around $200 as a unit. Samsung door bins typically list at $115 to $140 and are often out of stock.

If you can find the right original at a fair price, buy it. Find the model number first, because fridge makers use many similar-looking bins that do not interchange.

## Option 2: a used part

A used bin from a salvage seller or marketplace is cheaper, but its history is unknown. It may already have hairline cracks, and the seller may not know which models it fits. Shipping on a bulky bin can also eat the saving. Used makes sense when you can confirm the part number matches yours.

## Option 3: a printed bin

We print bins to order in PETG, a tough plastic that stays strong in the cold. We make the shape from your model number and photos, rather than selling a stocked part. A printed bin is a good fit when the original is out of stock or costs more than the repair is worth.

Printed does not mean identical. The surface shows fine print lines and the color is the nearest we can offer. We make no food-contact claims, so we suggest a printed bin for jars, bottles and packaged food, not loose items. We also do not claim it is an original part or that it is certified in any way.

## Comparison

Option | Typical price | Availability | Fit risk

Original part | About $115 to $200 or more, depending on model | Often out of stock | Lowest, if the part number is right

Used part | Typically lower, plus shipping | Hit or miss | Medium; condition unknown

Printed to order | From $55 to $65 for a typical bin | Made after you approve the quote, usually 5 to 10 business days | Low to medium; depends on your photos and model number

The prices for printed parts are starting points for a typical quote. The final price depends on the size and shape of your bin.

## How to decide

- Find your model number, usually on a sticker inside the fridge compartment.

- Search for the original part by that number and note the price and stock.

- If the original is under about half the cost of the appliance repair you are avoiding and in stock, buy it.

- If it is out of stock or too costly, request a printed quote and compare.

## What we need to quote a bin

Send the model number and photos of the broken bin and the door where it mounts. Put a ruler or a coin in the picture so we can read the scale, and photograph the bin from above and the side. For Whirlpool and KitchenAid style bins, see our Whirlpool and KitchenAid bin page. For Samsung, see the Samsung door bin page. If your fridge is another make, the custom part service covers it.

## Strength and honesty

Printed layers are weakest where they pull apart, so we orient the print so the main load runs along them, and we tell you if your bin is a poor candidate. Heavy items such as full milk jugs are the real test, so tell us what you plan to put in it.

## Ready to compare?

Send a photo and the model number through the request page. We reply within 24 hours on business days with a price, and you decide after seeing it.

## Need a replacement made?

Send a photo and the model number and we will quote within 24 hours on business days.

Request a quote

## Frequently asked questions

### Can a cracked fridge door bin be repaired instead of replaced?

Glue rarely holds, because the crack carries a load and cold plastic is brittle. A new or printed bin is usually the more reliable fix.

### Where is the model number on my fridge?

Usually on a sticker inside the fresh-food compartment, on a side wall or near the top. Photograph it and send it with the broken bin.

### Is a printed bin food safe?

We make no food-contact claims. Use it for jars, bottles and packaged food rather than loose food.

### How long does a printed bin take?

We quote within 24 hours on business days, then print it in 5 to 10 business days after you approve the quote.

# How to photograph a broken part so we can quote it

By PartRevive · 2026-10-21

Short answer: Photograph the broken part from the top, side and mounting end with a coin or ruler beside it, and add the model number. That is usually enough for us to quote within 24 hours on business days.

## The short answer

Four things get a quote fast: clear photos from several angles, a coin or ruler for scale, the model number of the machine, and the broken pieces if you still have them. Everything else we can ask about.

## What you need

- A phone camera.

- A coin or a ruler.

- A plain, light background such as a sheet of paper.

- Good light, ideally a window rather than the flash.

## Step 1: find the model number

The model number tells us exactly which machine the part belongs to. Look for a sticker or plate in these places.

- Fridges: inside the fresh-food compartment, on a side wall or near the top.

- Dryers and dishwashers: inside the door opening or on the back panel.

- Toolboxes: molded into the base or on the lid.

- RV windows: stamped on the frame, or sometimes not marked at all.

- Cars: the year, model and trim level, which is usually enough.

Photograph the sticker straight on, close enough to read the digits.

## Step 2: photograph the part itself

### Take at least four photos

- Top view: looking straight down, the whole part in frame.

- Side view: shows thickness and any hooks or tabs.

- Mounting end: the end that attaches to the machine, with holes or clips visible.

- The place it fits: the empty spot on the machine, so we see the space it fills.

### Always include scale

Put a coin or ruler right beside the part, on the same surface. Tell us which coin, for example a US quarter, which is 24.26 mm wide. A ruler laid flat is even better. A photo without scale forces us to guess, and a guess is how a part ends up too small.

## Step 3: add the broken pieces

If the part snapped, keep every piece. Photograph the broken faces, because they show how thick the part was and where it failed. A snap that is flat and clean tells us the load direction, which affects how we print the new one. Do not glue the pieces together before you photograph them.

## Step 4: measure the key sizes

If you have a ruler or a pair of calipers, add these notes in your message.

- The longest length.

- The width and thickness at the thinnest point.

- The distance between mounting holes.

- The diameter of a shaft or pin, if it fits on one.

Round to the nearest millimeter. If you do not have tools, skip this. The scale in the photo is enough for many parts.

## If you cannot remove the part

Sometimes the part is stuck, or removing it would break the machine. In that case, photograph it in place from several angles, with the coin held beside it, and measure what you can with a ruler. Tell us if you are unsure about how it comes off. We can often work out the hidden side from the visible one, and we tell you what we cannot see.

### If the part is missing entirely

If the part fell off years ago, photograph the empty space and anything that touches it: the pin it sat on, the slot it slid into, the parts either side. Add the model number and a short note on what the part does. A missing part is harder to quote than a broken one, but it is often still possible, and the quote says so plainly.

### Send more than you think you need

Extra photos cost you nothing and save a round of questions. If we can quote on the first reply, you get your answer within the 24 hours instead of waiting for a second exchange.

## Common mistakes

Mistake | Why it matters | Fix

No coin or ruler | We cannot read size | Add a coin beside the part

Photographed at an angle | Distorts shape | Shoot straight down for the top view

Dark or blurry shot | Hides edges and holes | Use window light and hold the phone steady

No model number | Hard to confirm the match | Photograph the machine's label

## What we can and cannot make

We print plastic parts up to 250 mm. We do not print food-contact or safety-critical parts, and we do not touch electrical parts. Read the printability checklist if you are unsure. For examples of what a finished quote looks like, see the custom part from a photo page.

## Step 5: send it

Use the request page. Include the brand and model, what the part does, and your location for shipping. We reply within 24 hours on business days with a quote, a question, or an honest no. If you approve the quote, printing and shipping usually take 5 to 10 business days.

## Need a replacement made?

Send a photo and the model number and we will quote within 24 hours on business days.

Request a quote

## Frequently asked questions

### How many photos should I send?

At least four: top, side, mounting end, and the place it fits on the machine. More is fine.

### What can I use for scale?

A coin or a ruler placed right beside the part. A US quarter is 24.26 mm wide.

### Where is the model number?

On a sticker or plate: inside the door for dryers and dishwashers, inside the compartment for fridges, or on the base of a toolbox.

### Should I glue the broken part first?

No. Keep the pieces separate and photograph the broken faces.

### What happens after I send the photos?

We reply within 24 hours on business days with a quote, a question, or an honest no.

## Related parts

-

Tools and toolbox parts

### Custom replacement part from a photo

Send us a photo of a broken or missing plastic part, with a coin or ruler beside it, and we quote a 3D-printed replacement...

From $35

# How to replace a broken RV screen door latch or handle

By PartRevive · 2026-10-21

Short answer: To replace a broken RV screen door latch, first work out whether it is a left-hand or right-hand door, then measure the distance between the mounting holes. If a stock kit does not match, we print an exact-fit paddle or handle in ASA from a photo, quoted within 24 hours on business days.

## The short answer

Most screen door latch failures come down to a cracked plastic paddle, a worn lever or a spring-return part that has given up. Before you buy anything, you need three facts: which hand the door is, how far apart the screw holes sit, and whether the broken part is sold on its own or only inside a full kit.

That last point matters. The paddle and lever can be hard to find on their own, and the small part you need is often not offered alone.

## Why screen door latches break

Screen door hardware sits in direct sun and gets used every day. Plastic paddles and levers typically become brittle with UV exposure, then crack at the pivot or where the screw passes through. The spring-return mechanism adds a small, repeated load every time someone walks in or out.

- A paddle that snaps off at its base is often a sign of aged plastic.

- A latch that works but will not return is often the spring part, not the handle.

- Stripped screw holes in thin door skin are a separate problem that a new latch will not fix.

## Step 1: identify left hand or right hand

Handedness trips up many first-time buyers. Stand outside the trailer, facing the screen door, and note which side the hinges are on. Many parts are made as a mirrored pair, so a right-hand handle will not work on a left-hand door even though the two look almost identical.

An easy check is to look at which way the paddle or lever points when the latch is at rest and which way you push it. If you are unsure, photograph the door from outside and from inside and we will read the hand from the pictures.

## Step 2: measure the hole spacing

Hole spacing is the single most useful measurement. Use a ruler or calipers and measure from the center of one mounting hole to the center of the next. Write the number down in millimeters or inches, and say which you used.

- Measure center to center between the two screw holes on the latch body.

- Measure the thickness of the door skin or frame where the latch mounts.

- Note the screw type and length if you still have the screws.

- Check whether the latch also has a strike plate on the frame, and photograph it.

## Kit, aftermarket or printed: how they compare

A full kit is the right answer when the whole latch is worn, or when you want everything new at once. A printed part makes sense when only the plastic paddle or lever has failed and the rest of the hardware is sound.

Option | Typical price | Fit | Material | Lead time

Zinc latch kit, third-party listing | $17.09 on Amazon (third-party seller) | Good if it matches your door hand and holes | Zinc | Varies by seller

Dealer or OEM part | Varies; may be discontinued | Matches the original if available | Original plastic or metal | Varies

Printed here | From $22 | Matched to your photo and measurements | ASA | 5 to 10 business days after approval

If a $17 kit fits your door, buy the kit. Our part is for the case where nothing on the shelf matches your hand or hole spacing, or where only one small piece is missing.

## Why we use ASA for a door in the sun

ASA is a plastic made for outdoor use, with good resistance to sun and heat. It suits a screen door latch that lives outside all summer. PETG is also a reasonable choice if the latch will be shaded. We will suggest the better one for your trailer when we quote.

## Related parts we make

While you are at the door, check the other plastic bits. A worn RV door holder catch lets the door swing in the wind; a typical store-bought 3-inch catch, such as the Camco listing at $8.59 on Ace Hardware, works for standard doors, and we can make one for odd shapes the generic part does not fit. Sun-baked RV window latches fail in the same way and are often sold only as an assembly. You can see the screen door part itself on the RV screen door latch page.

## Step 3: what to photograph

Good photos save a round of emails. Take them with a coin or ruler beside the part, in daylight, with the phone held straight on.

- The broken latch or handle from the front, with a coin or ruler in view.

- The back of the latch, showing the mounting holes and any spring.

- The door from outside, showing the hinge side.

- Any pieces that broke off, laid flat next to the ruler.

- The strike plate or catch on the door frame.

Send them on the request page, along with your trailer make and year if you know them. Our guide to photographing a broken part goes into more detail.

## What we do not promise

A printed latch is not an original part, and we are not affiliated with any trailer maker. We do not claim it is equal to the factory part. If a latch is a poor candidate for printing, for example because the body is cast metal, we say so rather than quote it.

Quotes arrive within 24 hours on business days. Once you approve, parts ship 5 to 10 business days after approval.

## Need a replacement made?

Send a photo and the model number and we will quote within 24 hours on business days.

Request a quote

### How do I tell if my RV screen door is left hand or right hand?

Stand outside facing the door and see which side the hinges are on. If you are unsure, send photos from outside and inside and we will work it out.

### What measurement matters most?

The center-to-center distance between the two mounting holes on the latch. Add the door skin thickness if you can.

### Is a kit cheaper than a printed part?

A zinc kit was listed at $17.09 on Amazon by a third-party seller, and our printed part starts from $22. A kit is the better buy if it fits your hand and holes.

### Which material do you use?

Usually ASA, which is made for sun and heat. We may suggest PETG for a shaded door.

### How long does it take?

We quote within 24 hours on business days, and parts ship 5 to 10 business days after approval.

# RV window latch replacement: a plain guide to your options

By PartRevive · 2026-10-21

Short answer: To replace a broken RV window latch, identify the window style, then choose an original assembly, a used part, or a printed latch. Printed latches from other sellers typically cost $7 to $24; we print in UV-resistant ASA and quote from $18 per latch within 24 hours.

## The short answer

An RV window latch is a small plastic part, but it is often not sold alone. You can replace it by buying the whole window assembly, finding a used latch, or having one printed in a sun-resistant plastic. A printed latch can be a way to get a working window without paying for an assembly.

## Why RV window latches break

RV windows face direct sun, heat and cold for years. UV light makes plastic brittle, and heat cycling in a closed, parked RV speeds it up. The latch then snaps the first time you push on it, often after a decade of normal use. The window frame is usually fine.

Elixir, Hehr and Kinro are three names you will see on many travel trailer and motorhome windows. We use those names only to describe what a part fits. We are not affiliated with any of them.

## Step 1: identify what you have

Start by looking at the latch and the window it came from.

- Look for a brand or number stamped on the frame or the latch.

- Note whether the window slides, tilts out, or hinges at the top.

- Check how the latch mounts: screws, a clip, or a pin through the frame.

- Photograph it from above and from the side with a coin beside it.

## Step 2: compare your options

Option | Typical price | Availability | Fit risk

Original latch or assembly | Varies; assemblies typically cost more than a latch | Often sold only as an assembly | Lowest, if the part number is right

Used latch | Typically low, plus shipping | Hit or miss | Medium; the plastic may already be aged

Printed in ASA | $7 to $24 from other printed sellers; from $18 here | Made to order, usually 5 to 10 business days after approval | Low to medium; depends on your photos

## Why the material matters

Many printed latches are made from PLA, a common hobby plastic that softens in a hot vehicle. On a sun-facing window that is the wrong choice. We print in ASA, which is made for sun and heat, so the new latch is better suited to sun and heat. See our RV window latch page for details.

### Strength in plain terms

A window latch holds a window closed against wind. It is not a lock and it does not hold a person's weight. Printed layers are weakest where they pull apart, so we orient the print so the main load runs along them.

## Step 3: get a printed latch

- Take the photos described above, with a coin or ruler in the shot.

- Send them through the request page, with the RV make and year if you know them.

- We reply within 24 hours on business days. We say yes, ask a question, or tell you honestly if the shape is a poor fit.

- If you approve the quote, we print and ship it, usually in 5 to 10 business days.

## If you also have a cabinet latch problem

The same heat that cracks window latches breaks cabinet latches. Some of those shapes are discontinued, such as the Newmar 020658A. A printed copy of that one sells for about $24 elsewhere, and we quote cabinet latches from $22. See the cabinet latch page.

## Tips to make the new latch last

- Do not force a stiff window. Clean and lubricate the track first.

- Order a spare for each window that has the same latch, since the others are the same age.

- Park with a sun cover where you can. UV is the main enemy of RV plastic.

## What to expect when the new latch arrives

Fit the latch before you tighten any screws fully. Check that it closes the window with a firm click and that the window does not rattle. If the fit is off by a millimeter or two, tell us what you see and send a photo of the problem. We would rather adjust than leave you with a latch that nearly works.

### Questions to ask any seller

- What plastic is it made from, and is it rated for sun and heat?

- How is the print oriented relative to the load?

- Will they confirm the fit from your photo before taking payment?

Those three answers tell you more than a price. A cheap latch in the wrong plastic can fail in the first hot summer, and then you are doing the job twice.

## Send a photo

If you are not sure what you have, send a photo anyway. We would rather tell you the part is not worth printing than quote a bad match. Use the request page to start.

## Need a replacement made?

Send a photo and the model number and we will quote within 24 hours on business days.

Request a quote

## Frequently asked questions

### Why did my RV window latch break?

UV light and heat make the plastic brittle over the years, so it snaps under normal use. The window frame is usually still fine.

### Can I buy just the latch?

Often the original is sold only as part of an assembly. Printed latches are one way to get the single part.

### What plastic should an RV latch be?

ASA, because it resists UV and heat. PLA softens in a hot vehicle, so we do not use it for RV parts.

### How much does a printed latch cost?

Other printed sellers charge roughly $7 to $24 per latch. We quote from $18 per latch, with lower per-unit prices for multiples.

# About PartRevive

Short answer: PartRevive is a new one-person shop, launched October 2026, that 3D-prints replacement plastic parts to order.

## Why this exists

A small plastic part breaks, and the maker sells only the whole assembly, or no longer sells it at all. We make the single part you need, in a material chosen for how it is used.

## How we work

- You send a photo and the model number.

- We quote within 24 hours on business days, including whether printing is a sensible fix.

- You approve, we design and print it, and we ship it. Lead time is 5 to 10 business days after approval.

We do not stock parts. Everything is made to order, up to about 250 mm.

## Materials

- PETG for general parts kept out of heat and direct sun

- ASA for sun and heat

- PA-CF (carbon-fiber nylon) for high loads

- TPU for flexible parts

## What we will not make

Safety-critical parts such as brake or steering components, battery contacts and other live electrical parts, children's items, and surfaces that touch food. We also do not claim our parts are equivalent to, or certified against, the original maker's part.

## Brands

We are not affiliated with any brand named on this site. Brand and model names identify fit only.

Request a quote

# Frequently asked questions

### How does PartRevive work?

Send a photo of the broken part, plus the brand and model it came from. We reply with a quote within 24 hours on business days. Once you approve it we design the part, print it, and ship it. Nothing is stocked; every part is made to order.

### How much does a replacement part cost?

Each part page shows a from-price for a typical quote. The final price depends on size, material and quantity, and we confirm it with you before anything is printed.

### How long does it take?

You get a quote within 24 hours on business days. Making and shipping takes 5 to 10 business days after approval.

### Is a 3D-printed part as strong as the original?

It depends on the material and the part. A part in a stronger material such as PA-CF can be stiffer than the original plastic, while a flexible TPU part will not be. We tell you honestly what to expect in the quote, and we do not claim equivalence with the original maker's part.

### What materials do you use?

We print in PETG, ASA, PA-CF (carbon-fibre nylon), TPU. PETG suits general indoor parts, ASA suits sun and heat, PA-CF suits high loads, and TPU suits flexible parts.

### What will you not make?

We do not make safety-critical parts such as brake or steering components, battery contacts or other live electrical parts, children's items, or surfaces that touch food. If you are unsure, ask and we will tell you straight.

### Are you affiliated with the brands on your site?

No. Brand and model names are used only to say what a part fits. We are an independent shop.

### How do I photograph and measure the broken part?

Photograph the part from two or three angles on a plain background, with a coin or ruler beside it for scale, and include the model number of the appliance, vehicle or tool. Keep the broken pieces; they help even if they are in several bits.

### What is the largest part you can make?

About 250 mm in the longest direction. Larger parts may be possible as an assembly; ask us.

### Where do you ship?

We currently serve customers in the United States.

Request a quote
